title: Anomalously enhanced lifetimes of low angular momentum Rydberg states in singly charged alkaline-earth metal ions
authors: Simon Euchner, Weibin Li, Igor Lesanovsky
abstract: Trapped ions excited to high-lying electronic states, so-called Rydberg states, open new opportunities for quantum simulation and quantum computing. Generally, the fidelity of quantum coherent operations critically depends on the longevity of Rydberg states. However, scaling laws predict that the lifetimes of Rydberg states in singly charged alkaline-earth metal ions are 16 times shorter, compared to their neutral atom counterparts. Here, we show that this is not generally the case. We report an anomalous lifetime enhancement of certain low angular momentum ionic Rydberg series by factors larger than eight. The anomaly is present at both zero and finite temperature, although it is caused by different mechanisms. At zero temperature, the anomalously enhanced lifetimes are caused by accidental cancellations of the relevant dipole transition matrix elements, while at room temperature the anomaly originates from the enlarged energetic separation of ionic Rydberg levels with respect to neutral-atom levels.
summary: This study analyzes the lifetimes of Rydberg states in singly charged alkaline-earth metal ions, finding that standard scaling laws fail to predict the longevity. The authors demonstrate anomalous lifetime enhancements at both zero and room temperatures, attributing the zero-T anomaly to matrix element cancellations and the room-T anomaly to increased energy level separation.
main_problem: The paper investigates the lifetimes of low angular momentum Rydberg states in singly charged alkaline-earth metal ions, challenging the prediction that these lifetimes should be significantly shorter than neutral atoms.
main_result: Anomalous lifetime enhancements (factors >8) are reported, attributed to accidental cancellations of dipole transition matrix elements at zero temperature and enlarged energetic level separations at room temperature.
method: Theoretical calculations using a single-electron model Hamiltonian, involving diagonalization of the Hamiltonian and calculating radiative and black-body radiation-induced decay rates.
model_or_system: The system involves trapped ions (e.g., Sr+, Rb) excited to high-lying Rydberg states. The dynamics are modeled using a single-electron Hamiltonian incorporating screening effects, and lifetimes are calculated for both zero and finite temperatures.
key_observables: Rydberg state lifetimes ($	au$), radiative decay rates ($	au_{	ext{rad}}^{-1}$), and black-body radiation (BBR) induced decay rates ($	au_{	ext{bbr}}^{-1}$).
important_parameters: Singly charged alkaline-earth metal ions ($	ext{Sr}^+, 	ext{Ca}^+$), principal quantum number ($n$), and temperature ($T=0$ vs $T=300	ext{ K}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a parametric model potential for the ion and assumes that the anomalous effects are dominated by matrix element cancellations or BBR coupling mechanisms.
figures_summary: Figures compare computed lifetimes for Rb and Sr+ across different quantum numbers, showing deviations from predicted scaling laws, and illustrate the relative contributions of spontaneous vs. BBR decay rates.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by contrasting predicted scaling laws with observed anomalies. It then details the theoretical mechanisms causing the enhancement at zero and finite temperatures, supported by extensive numerical calculations and comparisons with existing literature.
why_interesting: This work provides crucial insights into how core effects (like screening and specific matrix element cancellations) can fundamentally alter fundamental scaling predictions in highly excited atomic states, which is vital for designing robust quantum memory elements.
